cefrAlignment: B2 fits: items test word formation, tense and aspect (present perfect, passive continuous), linking devices and text-level coherence, which are typical of B2 grammatical range in workplace and academic texts.
examFidelity: TOEIC Part 5 and Part 6 items now each have one correct option. The TOEFL Complete the Words task now matches exams.ts: a paragraph of about 86 words with an intact first sentence, the second half of every second word missing, exactly 10 damaged words, and the larger half removed from odd-length words, as in the ETS sample.
fixes: Rebuilt the Complete the Words paragraph. The old one had 15 gaps, broke the every-second-word pattern after the 8th gap, was only about 50 words long, and cut 'sources' as 'sour__' (inconsistent with the larger-half rule). It now has exactly 10 gaps in an 86-word paragraph, with accepted answers for each.
Fixed the model example 'sev__' → 'se___' (seven; type 'ven'), so it follows the ETS deletion rule.
The Learn text now describes Complete the Words as in exams.ts (70–100 words, every second word, 10 words, larger half missing in odd-length words).
TOEIC Part 6 gap 4 had two defensible answers: 'Limited parking… so spaces must be reserved' is logical. Replaced the distractor 'so' with 'or' and explained why each wrong option fails.
Softened the farther/further explanation ('normally used only for physical distance') and covered every option.
The instructions now tell learners that the real test shows one space per missing letter.
openConcerns: The app's gap input cannot show one box per missing letter, and it accepts the whole word, so the drill is easier than the real TOEFL task. A UI option for letter-count boxes would improve fidelity.
Only one Part 6 sentence-insertion item is practised (plus one in the model). A specialist may want a second text.
learnerOutcome: Learners can use the words around a gap to choose word forms, tenses and linkers for TOEIC Parts 5–6, and can rebuild half-missing words in a TOEFL-style paragraph.
